cur:monumental2-tokali-adoration-magi.summary: The Virgin sits enthroned at the left holding the Christ Child on her lap, while the three Magi, crowned and richly dressed, advance in a tight group from the right bearing their gifts; Joseph and an angel stand behind. A Greek inscription runs across the blue sky above the figures.
facts: The Magi are shown as three ages of man (young, mature and old), a convention widely used in Byzantine art to suggest that all humanity comes to worship Christ.
cur:monumental2-tokali-adoration-magi.notes: The Commons file is unlabelled ('The magi. Fresco in Cappadocia', dated there to the 12th century) but is categorised among the Tokalı Kilise frescoes; the blue ground and style indicate the New Church. Location should be treated as probable.

princeton:54382.summary: Within a tiny dark mount, a carver has cut the head of Christ from a seed pod: the face is long and calm, framed by finely worked curling hair and a forked beard, with a thin band across the brow that may be the crown of thorns. The minute scale and naturalistic, European-style features make it a remarkable piece of devotional miniature work from South America.
facts: The carving is only about 3 × 2.6 cm.
Princeton records it as South American and probably a gift of Elroy Curtis (Class of 1900), from the collection of William E. Curtis.
princeton:54382.notes: The museum gives no date (its date range is 1–1954); the 'A.D. 500–1000' in our data is unfounded. The European iconography means it cannot predate the Spanish conquest, and the style suggests the 18th or 19th century; year 1850 is an approximate placeholder. Scripture omitted.
